{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693618682,"sessionID":"ses_e23ee9f5dffeQkoe7Kl8QZHyqS","part":{"id":"prt_1dc1359ed0016fD6S0wI59lXiM","messageID":"msg_1dc133998001WWrC4NQB9mUe0e","sessionID":"ses_e23ee9f5dffeQkoe7Kl8QZHyqS","type":"text","text":"The shift is over. By minute 120 all four customer-facing services were at a 0% error rate, with no throttles on and every service back to its normal replica count.\n\nThere were four separate causes. Three were present at the page and one started during the shift:\n\n1. **vouchers-svc, deploy v56** (minute −25): the new code reads `row[\"currency\"]` directly instead of falling back to EUR, so it errors whenever that field is missing. mobile-api was failing about 98% of requests. I rolled it back at minute 11.\n2. **bundles-svc, config cfg-42** (minute −20): it removed `orders.write` from the service's permissions. Failed calls were retried, which overloaded bundles-svc. I reverted the config at minute 20. The service stayed overloaded at about 40% errors afterwards, so I rejected 40% of its requests for about 6 minutes to stop the retries, then lifted that. It recovered without extra replicas.\n3. **ledger-db, deploy v95** (minute −25): it divided cache entry lifetimes by 600, so entries expired before they were read. Through labels-svc and audit-svc, this caused the 4.4% errors on web-storefront and partner-api. That cost about $510 a minute, the largest loss of the shift. ledger-db was already at 88% CPU, so I added replicas first (8 to 12) so the failures during the rollback wouldn't overload it. I rolled it back at minute 49 and returned it to 8 replicas when it finished. All edge errors were at 0% by minute 56.\n4. **inventory-db, config cfg-6** (started at minute 61): it cut the rate limit from 5000 to 50 per second, which took mobile-api back up to about 82% errors through seo-svc. I reverted it at minute 85 and rejected 40% of its requests for about 5 minutes to clear the retry overload. It was clean from minute 91.\n\nloyalty-svc kept a high-CPU alert all shift. Nothing calls it, so it can't affect customers and I left it alone. I also skipped the other recent changes I checked. Their diffs looked harmless, so I applied no mitigations that weren't needed.\n\nThe extra costs were small: four extra ledger-db replicas for about 12 minutes, and a few minutes of rejected traffic on mobile-api.","time":{"start":1794693618157,"end":1794693618678}}}
